english_paragraphs: OK, often said to be the planet's most frequently spoken word, began as a newspaper gag. From 1838 abbreviations were all the vogue in Boston's papers, and the craze turned comic through deliberate misspellings: O.W. for 'oll wright', K.Y. for 'know yuse'. The humour lay in the persona of an uneducated bumpkin.

On 23 March 1839 a Boston Morning Post satire took a swipe at a contemporary, the Providence Journal, over a mock society parodying an ordinance against ringing dinner bells. It carried the first known 'o.k.', glossed as 'all correct'. The letters stood for a knowingly illiterate 'oll korrect'. The presumed writer was the editor, Charles Gordon Greene.

Partisan politics propagated the letters nationwide. In 1840 Martin Van Buren, the incumbent president, sought re-election. His New York backers, punning on his nickname 'Old Kinderhook', after his birthplace, formed the Democratic O.K. Club, making the letters a double-meaning slogan. That November William Henry Harrison unseated him, 234 electoral votes to 60.

On 30 March 1840 the New York Morning Herald printed a fabricated smear: the former president Andrew Jackson, a supposedly inept speller, had marked paperwork O.K., for 'Ole Kurrek'. Jackson spelled reasonably well and never marked documents O.K. Within about twenty years, people did so in earnest. The bogus notation was merely premature.

Rival stories offered exotic pedigrees: Choctaw 'okeh' and Greek 'ola kala'. Authoritative dictionaries favoured Choctaw as late as 1961. In 1963–64 the linguist Allen Walker Read excavated the neglected Boston provenance from archival newspapers in six influential American Speech articles. Most dictionaries now embrace his derivation, a pedigree of bad spelling and dinner-bell satire.
chinese_paragraphs: OK常被称为世界上最常说的词，起初却只是报纸上的一个笑话。从1838年起，波士顿报纸流行起缩写，又故意把词拼错来逗乐，例如用O.W.代表“oll wright”，用K.Y.代表“know yuse”。笑点在于装出一个没受过教育的乡下人的口吻。
1839年3月23日，《波士顿晨邮报》刊出一篇讽刺文，借一个戏仿禁敲开饭铃法令的虚构社团，挖苦同期的《普罗维登斯日报》。文中出现了已知最早的“o.k.”，并解释为“all correct”，即完全正确。这两个字母实际取自故意写错的“oll korrect”。文章的推定作者是编辑查尔斯·戈登·格林。
党派政治把这两个字母传播到了全国。1840年，在任总统马丁·范布伦谋求连任。他在纽约的支持者拿他根据出生地得来的绰号“Old Kinderhook”玩双关，成立民主党O.K.俱乐部，让OK成了一句兼具两重意思的竞选口号。当年11月，威廉·亨利·哈里森以234张选举人票对60张击败了他。
1840年3月30日，《纽约先驱晨报》刊出一则捏造的抹黑故事，说前总统安德鲁·杰克逊不擅拼写，曾在公文上批注O.K.，代表“Ole Kurrek”。实际上，杰克逊的拼写并不差，也从未这样批过文件。不过，在大约二十年内，人们果真开始认真使用这种批注。那种虚构的批注用法，不过是比实际流行早了一些。
其他词源说法另寻异域来历，例如乔克托语的“okeh”和希腊语的“ola kala”。直到1961年，权威词典仍倾向于乔克托语说。1963至1964年，语言学家艾伦·沃克·里德从报纸档案中发掘出被忽略的波士顿起源，并在《美国语言》发表了六篇影响深远的文章。如今，大多数词典都接受他的词源解释：这个词的身世，原来连着故意错拼和开饭铃讽刺文。

illustration_prompt:
Create a single publication-quality landscape 3:2 narrative illustration for an adult illustrated English-reading booklet. Finished standalone artwork, not a book mockup, not a collage of multiple unrelated panels. Sophisticated contemporary editorial gouache and watercolor, carefully controlled colored-pencil accents, velvety matte paint, subtle warm paper texture, soft natural daylight. Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Detailed but uncluttered. Historically and scientifically appropriate objects, clothing and setting. Show the particular article's pivotal event or mechanism rather than a generic portrait or generic textbook symbols. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. For disasters, emphasize the setting, evidence or human response without graphic suffering. For uncertain scientific claims, depict the observations and investigation without presenting debated mechanisms as proven. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Do not render invisible forces as literal magic. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet.

ARTICLE-SPECIFIC SCENE:
A small Boston newspaper printing office in 1839. One amused young editor in restrained early-19th-century clothing leans over a wooden composing desk while a skilled typesetter selects two tiny pieces of metal movable type, their printing faces turned away from the viewer so absolutely no letters are visible. The central story is an intentionally playful newspaper abbreviation taking shape through the physical craft of typesetting. A modest hand-operated press and one freshly printed sheet viewed from its completely blank reverse side provide the only secondary details. No modern keyboard, no campaign posters, no readable type, no pseudo-writing, no visible OK lettering. Respectful adult figures with natural hands and a quiet shared smile rather than caricature; ivory, sage and a little muted terracotta.
approved_summary: 1838年起，波士顿报纸流行故意拼错词再缩写；1839年出现已知最早的“o.k.”。
o.k.取自all correct的故意错拼oll korrect，意为“完全正确”，笑点在模仿文盲口吻。
1840年，范布伦阵营以绰号Old Kinderhook的缩写OK，兼指他本人和“完全正确”，用作竞选口号。
范布伦败选，OK仍流传；杰克逊用它批文件的传闻是捏造，但约二十年内人们已认真如此批注。
语言学家里德于1963至1964年查旧报，重建波士顿词源；多数词典采纳，取代早先乔克托语等说法。
